proved: For each fixed B0 coarse class sigma, the known P7-free List-3-Colouring algorithm can be used as an auxiliary structural split into at most three stable sets R_i, without committing those colors to the global extension.
For every i and every k>=1, every induced P_k in I_{sigma,i} lifts to an induced P_k in the original graph G by arbitrary choice of one representative from every component-node.
Each I_{sigma,i} is bipartite by construction, so the existing Lozin-Zamaraev P7-free bipartite chain decomposition applies separately to each layer.
imported_not_reproved: P7-free List-3-Colouring is polynomial-time solvable and returns an explicit coloring if one exists.
Every P7-free bipartite graph is chain-decomposable.
The Lozin-Zamaraev decomposition tree has linear size; for n>=3, at most 8n-17 nodes.
The known structure implies bounded mim-width with an efficiently findable corresponding decomposition for P7-free bipartite graphs.
firewalls: Auxiliary layer colors are not committed extension colors.
Three separately tractable incidence layers do not imply their union has bounded mim-width.
Linear-size decomposition trees do not imply polynomially many proof-relevant shared-component boundary states.
No synchronization DP is constructed in B1A.
No B1B/module-transfer/broad-B1 work is performed here.
No full L2 repair, Lemma 11 P7 lift, polynomial P7-free 4-Coloring algorithm, or P=NP proof follows from B1A alone.
